title: Create and Publish Hardware-Specific Performance Profiles for Model Onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: produce, validate, and publish hardware-specific performance profiles for newly onboarded models and add version-pinning metadata so customers get deterministic behavior. Deliverables: (1) canonical perf profile JSONs for A100 (40GB/80GB variants), H100, L40S, and MI300; (2) automated benchmark harness integration and CI job; (3) model-catalog entries that include model_version -> profile_id mapping and recommended runtime flags (batching, quantization knobs, kernel hints); (4) docs and migration notes for Dedicated/Private customers. Profiles must include P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec for representative prompts, peak GPU memory footprints, recommended max_batch, kv_cache behavior, and quantization compatibility notes.
acceptance_criteria: Profiles published for at least 8 most-used models in catalog across A100/H100/L40S/MI300
Automated benchmark job passes nightly with <10% variance alerts and artifacts stored in S3 perf-archives
Model catalog shows version pin mapping and UI surfaces profile id and recommended flags
Runtime reads profile_id from model metadata and applies pinned kernel/quantization settings in canary rollout
Docs and migration notes published to Confluence and linked from Console model card

2026-03-11 - Omar Rodriguez: Initial benchmark harness merged (GH PR #5872). Harness supports variable seq_len, warmup tokens, and automatic kv_cache snapshotting. First runs on A100-80GB show expected throughput for gpt-neox variants.

2026-03-14 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Reviewed and requested explicit feature flags for version pinning behavior (pin_latest_patch vs pin_exact), and API contract for model_catalog.profile_id must be immutable once published for a given model_version.
2026-03-14 - Omar Rodriguez: Added CI nightly job (ci/perf-hw-nightly) and alert rule in Grafana for >10% regression. Re-running H100 tests with NVLink nodes.
Pending - Need design review for Console UI notes and approval from Security for S3 artifact retention policy (>90 days).
notes: Key trade-offs: (1) We will publish two profile tiers per hardware (low-latency vs cost-optimized) to allow customers to pick tradeoffs without per-customer tuning. (2) MI300 ROCm quirks require retaining a small set of fallback kernels; this increases our artifact size (~30MB per profile) but avoids customer regressions. (3) Version pinning model: model_catalog will expose 'pinned_version' attribute and 'profile_id' that runtime will honor for dedicated/private runs; hosted API will honor profile_id unless overridden by admin policy.
